date: Nov 18, 2026 · Week 2 / Day 3 · Decision-driven meetings and tradeoffs

cards.title: What must we decide today?
cards.question: A PCIe Gen5 review has 12 plots and 20 minutes. What single decision belongs on the agenda?
cards.selfCheck: Frame the choice: accept current margin, authorize a layout change, or hold signoff. Exercise: open in 20 seconds with decision, deadline and consequence of delay.
cards.prompt: Role-play a time-boxed PCIe Gen5 release review. Make me open with a precise decision and challenge vague agendas.

cards.title: Separate reversible from costly
cards.question: A via-backdrill ECO may recover 0.7 dB but risks a three-day board slip. What can be decided now?
cards.selfCheck: Separate a reversible simulation/prototype step from an irreversible fab release. Exercise: recommend the smallest commitment that preserves the decision window.
cards.prompt: Coach me through a via-backdrill ECO decision under schedule pressure. Test my reasoning about reversibility, evidence and deadlines.

cards.title: Stop debating the wrong plot
cards.question: EM and TDR teams dispute a 2 Ω impedance difference. How do you keep the meeting productive?
cards.selfCheck: Agree on the decision tolerance first, then reference planes, bandwidth and a correlation owner. Exercise: ask one question that determines whether the mismatch changes signoff.
cards.prompt: Act as conflicting EM and lab leads. Challenge me to redirect a technical argument toward the acceptance criterion and decisive experiment.

cards.title: Trade droop against schedule
cards.question: A 19 MHz PDN peak could violate transient droop, but a capacitor ECO threatens layout freeze. How do you align teams?
cards.selfCheck: Quantify droop against the actual load transient; compare ECO and validation paths with power, layout and program leads. Exercise: state a conditional recommendation with one owner and trigger.
cards.prompt: Simulate a cross-functional PDN meeting. Press me to balance load-transient evidence, mitigation cost and signoff risk without false certainty.

cards.title: Close with a real choice
cards.question: A 3 dB NEXT miss remains after two mitigation proposals. How do you end the review in 30 seconds?
cards.selfCheck: State the preferred option, residual risk, decision authority, due date and fallback if evidence fails. Exercise: deliver a concise closeout that names what would change your recommendation.
cards.prompt: Evaluate my 30-second NEXT review closeout as a Principal Engineer. Score decision clarity, tradeoff, uncertainty, accountable owner and fallback.
